items.title: The Hindu right in trouble
items.description: HAVING prospered abroad as an unbridled organisation flaunting different names and profiles for decades, the RSS seems to be in trouble in western cities and townships where unusual rage is surfacing at its documented hatred of Muslims and Christians. RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat’s visit to the US and Canada has come at a fraught time in the organisation’s global and domestic trajectory. The timing of this change in attitude coincides with a youth movement questioning the ideological fundamentals of the Modi government at home and decline of Israel as a morally tenable entity in the comity of nations. Israel’s fondness for India’s right-wing Hindu establishment has collaterally damaged India’s reputation as an old comrade in much of Asia, Africa and Latin America. Not quite flattering also is the reality of Pakistan’s rise as a widely wooed global partner with India painting itself into a diplomatic corner. When a frustrated Donald Trump yelled at Israel for becoming friendless and hated by everyone, Benjamin Netanyahu smiled back, saying he still had India for a friend. The backhanded compliment isn’t lost on the world at large. Where Pakistan is headed, India once claimed the high ground — the reliable friend ready to help untangle strategic and diplomatic knots world leaders needed to fix urgently. There was a time when leaders sought out India to intervene as an honest broker to wind down the traumatic Korean conflict, and they remained grateful that Nehru stepped in. There was a time when Indira Gandhi was urged by the Non-Aligned Movement to broker peace in the lacerating Iran-Iraq war. She dispatched senior diplomat Romesh Bhandari to placate the warring arch-foes as only a trusted Indian envoy could. And though the war eventually ended when a US warship shot down an Iranian Airbus packed with Dubai shoppers, India’s helping hand continued to be valued in the entire region. Today, the world may be interested in India’s lucrative market, but sans the respect India once commanded. There were Indian stowaways slinking out abroad even then, but they were never repatriated in handcuffs and fetters as Trump did with Indian citizens recently, even though Narendra Modi had canvassed support for his re-election in 2020. The RSS prides itself as a shadowy unregistered paramilitary body, whereas even the Nazis were a registered party. The RSS prides itself as a shadowy unregistered paramilitary body, whereas even the Nazis were a registered party. Critics point to its opaque financial resources at home and abroad. Those resources may have come under a cloud on two fronts. The opposition in India is demanding the group’s registration amid calls for transparency, which the RSS is assiduously resisting. Abroad, Trump has increased the visa fee to impossible figures for IT professionals to seek, and IT professionals are known to be the mainstay of RSS sympathisers and its finances in the US. How has the RSS stayed popular among the Indian diaspora was a question that a huge number of protesters in the US and Canada were asking ahead of and during Bhagwat’s visit. It rode piggyback with the powerful Israel lobby. But Christian Zionists and Jewish Zionists are under attack from within the Democratic and Republican establishments with Zohran Mamdani and Tucker Carlson being the tip of the iceberg. The consequent decline of Israel’s prowess is not good news for the RSS. Bhagwat’s reportedly conciliatory tone during his New York meeting presaged a looming crisis for the group in its various avatars. At the public meeting, he claimed that Hindus who wish to see Muslims out of India would cease to be Hindus if they did so. The comments were borrowed from a brainstorming meeting he organised in Delhi in 2018. Did that stop the bloodcurdling assaults on Muslims and Christians or the Dalits from Hindutva zealots? No. Even as Bhagwat was in New York or preparing to get there, the ground reality in India defied his claims. A new law in Maharashtra was being unveiled for Christians visiting the church to fill out a form to say they were not being coerced to convert. Is there a similar law for those forced or lured to convert to Hinduism? Around then the decks were also being cleared to free the Hindutva fanatic from jail who had burnt alive the Australian priest and caregiver Graham Steines and his two sons in their jeep in 1990. Two faux Hindu gurus jailed for rape, with one sentenced also for murder, are enjoying paroles and furloughs at will, while intellectual dissenters like Umar Khalid are languishing in prison, with no sign of a trial starting soon. Nehru used to say that the RSS was not a trustworthy organisation. Its leaders said one thing and did another. For example, the RSS distanced itself from Gandhi’s killer Godse but distributed sweets at the assassination, according to Sardar Patel. Modi, an RSS man did one better. He freed Samjhauta Express terror bomb accused Sadhvi Pragya from jail, made her an MP and then watched her praising Godse as a hero for killing Gandhi. Bhagwat reportedly told the Delhi brainstorming that some parts of former RSS chief Golwalkar’s book needed to be discarded. Let’s check it out. In Chapter V of his book We or Our Nationhood Defined , Golwalkar says: “The non-Hindu peoples in Hindustan must either adopt the Hindu culture and language, must learn to respect and hold in reverence Hindu religion, must entertain no idea but those of the glorification of the Hindu race and culture, ie, of the Hindu nation and must lose their separate existence to merge in the Hindu race, or may stay in the country, wholly subordinated to the Hindu Nation, claiming nothing, deserving no privileges, far less any preferential treatment — not even citizen’s rights.” What else is being pursued over the last 12-plus years? If Bhagwat is trying to rewrite the Golwalkar book, it indicates two possibilities. One, the RSS has gone fundamentally at loggerheads with the Modi government. Two, the RSS is in serious trouble. The writer is Dawn’s correspondent in Delhi. jawednaqvi@gmail.com Published in Dawn, September 1st, 2026

items.title: Liquidité bancaire : le besoin des banques recule à 125,7 MMDH en juillet
items.description: Le besoin en liquidité des banques s'est situé, en juillet dernier, à 125,7 milliards de dirhams (MMDH) en moyenne hebdomadaire, après 127,3 MMDH en juin, selon la Direction des études et des prévisions financières (DEPF). Dans ce contexte, la Banque Centrale a réduit le volume de ses injections de liquidité qui s'est établi en moyenne hebdomadaire à 144,1 MMDH, après 152,4 MMDH en juin, fait savoir la DEPF dans sa récente note de conjoncture. Les interventions de Bank Al-Maghrib ont porté, essentiellement, sur les avances à 7 jours (48,9 MMDH), les opérations de pensions livrées à 1 et 3 mois (48,9 MMDH) et les opérations de prêts garantis accordés dans le cadre des programmes de soutien au financement de la TPME – très petite, petite et moyenne entreprise (46,2 MMDH). S'agissant du volume moyen des transactions interbancaires, il s'est accru de 52,8%, par rapport au mois précédent, pour atteindre 3,3 MMDH au titre du mois de juillet dernier. Quant au taux interbancaire moyen pondéré au jour le jour (TIMPJJ), il se maintient depuis le 20 mars 2025 en évolution quasi-stable, alignée sur le taux directeur, s'établissant en moyenne à 2,25%. items.title: The golden goose
items.description: IT might be an odd week to write about journalism and indulge in some navel gazing, for much has happened in recent days to keep everyone occupied. From the Imran Khan health saga to tragedies that have left most gasping, with the fire at Pims and the murder of Hina Javed — whose husband has been arrested — in Pindi. And this was just in the twin cities. There was more such news from elsewhere — the rape and murder of a child in Haripur and the broader insecurity faced by people living in parts of KP and Balochistan. But it has to be said that the two incidents in Islamabad and Pindi — the power centre of this country — forced the state and society to pay attention. Indeed, at one level, one welcomed the fact that there had been little effort to stop the wall-to-wall coverage of and commentary on these two incidents. After a long time, it seemed as if journalists reported, commented and spoke without looking over their shoulder. So unusual was the experience that it was discussed in more than one newsroom, as insignificant hacks wondered what had happened and why there was some space. After all, now we live in a world where so much of what is happening in the country is a ‘red line’ — from the trees in Islamabad to incidents in our ‘invisible’ provinces to angry protests. Most of it is now left unreported. It is uncovered only by those who are willing to turn into Sherlock Holmes, trawling through social media for ‘events’. Simply the ‘what and when’ is becoming the holy grail. For the television channels beamed into our homes and the newspapers delivered to our phones have learnt that they can only print all the news considered fit to print by the powerful in Pakistan. And this has had an impact on the media industry in ways that are yet to be understood and analysed. Most media owners are no longer interested in investing in human resource. At the most basic level is the credibility gap issue and how it is adding, perhaps, to the shift of people to social media platforms for news. I use the word ‘perhaps’ because it is something I encounter anecdotally. People are moving to social media to learn about the issues no longer covered by the mainstream press. Part of it might be because digital platforms are now providing more innovation in content than the mainstream — for instance, the former now provide space for longer and more meaningful conversations than the same hurried, oft-repeated debate that has become the hallmark of lazy television journalism. Light, satirical commentary on politics is now also more readily available on the newer platforms. But this growth of the social media is now also changing trends within the industry where most acceptable ‘stories’ now make their way to platforms other than the mainstream press. Consider the story about Imran Khan first being taken to hospital for treatment. It came via a vlogger/ journalist on his YouTube show. Similarly, a podcast owned by Geo News disclosed that some IPP parliamentarians are drawing closer to PML-N and might even join it. And even more recently, the news of Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari’s possible engagement was made public in a YouTube conversation before it reached the mainstream. Even before these incidents, the story about Mohammad Zubair meeting the then army chief on behalf of Maryam Nawaz and Nawaz Sharif was provided on social media; in hindsight, it seems the news in this case may have been provided by the powers that be. These are some examples of stories which could have been reported by the mainstream media but were not. In some cases, it can be argued the podcasters preferred to use their personal platforms rather than the ones they are employed at. But can it explain all the cases? And it is also noteworthy that employers no longer feel the need to curb their employees on individual platforms. For in an industry where owners no longer care about audiences and are busy making money from government revenue (which is linked to docility rather than journalism), few are interested in either the quality of programmes or of what the anchors are doing outside of the show. Because nothing matters other than sanitised mindless shows and reporting which ensures generous revenue and no official reprimand. This is also why news channels no longer show any of the angst or energy in terms of reporting or content as was the hallmark of the earlier years. Programming has become monotonous; there is little innovation, and field reporting now takes place once there is some push from up above (and I don’t mean the management). Owners are busy counting ad revenue, access and favours and the ones in power are busy patting themselves on the back for having controlled the narrative. And if the people are no longer buying it, the echo chamber doesn’t let anyone find out. But there is an even more serious angle to this. Most media owners are no longer interested in investing in human resource for it is no longer needed as such. Who needs reporters, when reporting simply creates problems? Why bother hiring senior editorial people when stories no longer need to be vetted? And none of this affects the bottom line? Because content and reporting has little to do with how much money can be made. This is why nearly every other day comes the news of one channel or another firing people. It’s not random and neither is it whimsical. It reflects the priorities of an industry whose economic model is not linked to the quality of its output. Soon the industry might be tempted to replace news and programme hosts with AI-generated ones, if the latter come cheap enough and can be controlled. But I wonder if anyone has bothered to think about a day when the media loses its nuisance value entirely. Will the moolah still continue to flow into the coffers of the mainstream? Or will it simply fade into oblivion? The writer is a journalist. Published in Dawn, September 1st, 2026

items.title: PTI challenges govt claims about Imran’s incarceration
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Rejecting the government’s claims about Imran Khan as “misleading, fabricated and incorrect”, PTI leaders on Monday painted a sorry picture of the conditions he endures in prison. Last week, after an interview with Imran’s sons was broadcast during the Lord’s Test, the Ministry of Information issued a detailed statement, which was released on social media and sent to the foreign press. It claimed that Imran was “not a person held under executive detention” and that he had been incarcerated based on multiple convictions following judicial proceedings, noting that the PTI founder “remains entitled to pursue all remedies available to him under Pakistani law”. “His imprisonment is governed by the Pakistan Prison Rules, applicable judicial directions and security arrangements appropriate to a high-profile prisoner,” the statement read. Salman Akram Raja says court orders not being followed; lawyers not allowed to interact with their client even during trial The information ministry also rejected allegations that Imran was being subjected to “punitive solitary confinement, cruelty or deprivation”, stating that visits, phone calls, reading materials and home-cooked meals, among other amenities, were available to him. “His accommodation includes an exclusive seven-cell compound with sleeping, sanitation and exercise facilities,” the ministry said. However, speaking at a press conference on Monday, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja rejected all the claims. “The major grievance regarding Imran Khan and Bushra Bibi is that, for the last 15 months since March 2025, there has been a judgement of the Islamabad High Court that Imran and his wife be allowed to meet family members at least twice a week, but it is not being implemented,” he said. “The court also allowed meetings with lawyers, but they were not allowed. Meetings with Imran’s sisters were also severely restricted and, after October 2025, meetings with his sisters were stopped . “In November 2025, one sister, Dr Uzma, was allowed to meet Imran. Moreover, the Supreme Court of Pakistan ordered that Imran Khan be shifted to Shifa Interna­tional Hospital, but that order was also not implemented. This amounts to denial of Imran’s rights and the rights of his sisters,” he added. Mr Raja said nearly 300 cases had been filed against Imran, yet his lawyers were not allowed to meet him. “Only one lawyer, Salman Safdar, was allowed to meet him, but he did not meet him as Imran Khan’s lawyer; he met him as a court-appointed amicus. So the report stating that Imran Khan has been allowed to meet family and friends is fabricated,” he claimed. He said contempt petitions had also been filed against the Adiala jail administration for not allowing meetings with lawyers and family members. “Imran Khan has been in prison since 2023 and several cases against him have been tried within the jail premises. I repeat that from October 2025 to Aug 18, 2026, no meetings [apart from Dr Uzma] with Imran Khan were allowed, so he was in solitary confinement,” he said. Mr Raja claimed that Imran Khan was not even allowed to talk to anyone in the jail. “No facility is being given to him to punish him further. Imran has been separated from other co-accused persons and now his trial is being conducted through a video call made through a mobile phone. “Imran Khan cannot communicate with his lawyers or advise them during trials. If the judge and lawyers went to Adiala jail, they would be able to communicate with Imran Khan, but even that is not being allowed,” he explained. Sardar Latif Khosa said one of the greatest cricketers of all time was suffering in Pakistan. Replying to questions, the PTI secretary general said there was unity within the party, contrary to rumours about rifts. “We urge the Supreme Court to take notice of the disregard of its orders,” he said. Published in Dawn, September 1st, 2026

items.title: AJK govt announces phased restoration of internet services
items.description: MUZAFFARABAD: The Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) government has announced a phased restoration of internet services across the region, with broadband and cellular data services to resume fully in some districts while access will remain restricted to educational institutions and banks in others. The Home Department, in a notification issued on Sunday, directed the secretary of the Ministry of Interior to initiate restoration of broadband and cellular data services from Monday (Aug 31) according to a district-wise schedule. Under the schedule, full broadband and cellular data services will be restored in Neelum district, including Upper and Lower Neelum, as well as Leepa Valley and Haveli district. Broadband services will also be restored throughout Bhimber and Mirpur districts. In Muzaffarabad district, broadband access will be confined to educational institutions — schools, colleges and universities — and banks. The same arrangement will apply in Jhelum Valley. In Bagh district, broadband services will be available only to educational institutions and banks within the municipal limits of Bagh and Dhirkot. Similarly, in Kotli district, broadband access will be restricted to educational institutions and banks, except in Sehnsa, Sarsawa and Tattapani where services will remain shut. No internet services will be restored in Rawalakot and Sudhnoti districts, where the suspension will continue. Bankers in the capital welcomed the restoration, saying it would ease pressure on branches that had been handling a heavy volume of customers in the absence of digital banking facilities. Ordinary citizens, however, expressed disappointment over the limited scope of the restoration, particularly those dependent on the internet for their livelihoods. Faisal Javed, president of the Association of Pharmacies and Medical Stores, said the suspension had severely disrupted electronic payments, leaving both traders and customers in difficulty. Internet services were suspended across AJK on June 5 amid a law and order situation following the government’s decision to proscribe the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC). Published in Dawn, September 1st, 2026

items.title: Husband cannot reclaim dower gold as Khula compensation, LHC rules
items.description: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) has ruled that a husband is not entitled to reclaim gold ornaments listed as dower in a Nikahnama (marriage contract) as consideration for Khula (dissolution of marriage) sought by his wife. Justice Raheel Kamran passed the judgement while disposing of four connected petitions arising from a matrimonial dispute between Dr Rukhsana Kausar and Shahid Nazeer. Both parties had challenged the findings of a Muzaffargarh sessions court concerning gold ornaments and other matters, including maintenance, dowry and ownership of the couple’s house. The marriage was dissolved through Khula in 2012. The family court initially held that the wife was required to return the dower received as Badl-i-Khula (compensation for Khula), while other disputes, including maintenance, dowry articles, gold ornaments and delivery expenses, remained pending. In 2018, the family court partly decreed the suit, awarding maintenance and ordering recovery of dowry articles. It also directed the wife to return 11 tolas of gold, or its value, to the husband. The appellate court upheld these findings in 2020, reducing only the annual increase in the minor child’s maintenance from 15 to 10 pc. On maintenance, Justice Kamran upheld the concurrent findings, noting that the husband had withheld his complete salary record and produced only a certificate showing his basic pay. The courts were therefore entitled to draw an adverse inference regarding his actual earning capacity. The judge also noted that the husband’s brother had testified that he owned a Honda Civic, further undermining his claim of limited means. The court held that it would not permit a “financially capable parent” to understate his resources to reduce his obligations towards his child. Regarding the matrimonial house, the judge upheld findings that the wife’s father, who was working abroad at the time, had financed its entire purchase through a documented chain of banking transactions. Bank officials corroborated the transactions, and their testimony remained largely unchallenged during cross-examination. Since the husband had never actually paid for the house despite its inclusion in the dower, the judge held that it could not be reclaimed as Badl-i-Khula. He also upheld the wife’s subsequent transfer of the house to her father and the decree granting him possession. On the claim for 11 tolas of gold, Justice Kamran found that the lower courts had erred by treating the absence of documentary evidence as decisive while overlooking corroborating circumstances. Given the husband’s established financial incapacity, the judge held that it was more probable that the gold, too, had been financed by the wife’s father. “Consequently, the respondent cannot claim return of the said ornaments as Badl-i-Khula,” the judge held, because they did not represent dower financed or paid for by him from his own resources. Regarding 22 tolas of dowry gold, the judge upheld the findings against the wife, noting that she had never claimed the jewellery was forcibly taken from her. Her inconsistent accounts about when she left the matrimonial home, coupled with her refusal to produce a video of her sister’s wedding showing her wearing jewellery after leaving her husband’s home, also supported an adverse inference. Justice Kamran upheld the dismissal of the wife’s Rs63,000 claim for maternity/delivery expenses. Published in Dawn, September 1st, 2026

items.title: Trump vows to hit Iran hard after first exchanges of fire in a month
items.description: US President Donald Trump threatened further strikes against Iran on Monday after the first exchange of direct attacks in a month, raising tensions in a conflict that had recently shifted into an economic standoff. Iran launched missiles overnight at two US air bases in Jordan in response to a US attack on Iran's Larak Island, where Washington said it had struck Iranian launchers firing mines into the Strait of Hormuz. "We're going to hit them hard," a Fox News reporter quoted Trump as later telling the channel. "There will be a response." Trump said US forces allowed one Iranian missile to pass through air defenses overnight after determining it would not hit anything, while the other incoming missiles were intercepted. Separately, Trump told reporters in the Oval Office that the renewed strikes did not signal a return to full-scale war, describing Iran as a "failed nation" whose economy and military had been severely degraded. "That doesn't mean we won't smack them. We'll see what happens." A senior Iranian source told Reuters the overnight exchanges of fire, the first since late July, were a "limited and contained confrontation" but said Tehran would deliver a harsh response if attacked again. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called for maximum restraint following the resumption of hostilities over the weekend between the US and Iran and encouraged a return to diplomatic talks that would lead to a settlement to help restore stability in the region, his spokesperson Stephane Dujarric said Monday. Piling on economic pressure The renewed military exchanges came as Washington has stepped up economic pressure on Tehran and its business partners, imposing "secondary sanctions" on third countries that buy Iranian oil. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that Iran was "lashing out" now because the new sanctions were taking a toll on its economy. Bessent told Reuters on Sunday that new secondary sanctions were likely to be unveiled weekly in the effort to pressure Iran, with an initial focus on banks. The latest escalation has also heightened concerns over shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global energy transit route. Iranian state TV quoted Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps as saying a supertanker had caught fire and been brought to a halt after being struck by two naval mines in the south of the Strait of Hormuz. The US military later denied the claim. Over the past month, Washington has hoped a blockade of Iranian ports will inflict enough economic damage to force Iran to comply with US demands. Tehran, meanwhile, has maintained that the Strait of Hormuz is shut and will reopen only under its supervision. The number of visible commodity vessels transiting the strait dropped to five per day over the weekend, data from commodities firm Kpler showed. A tanker has reported being struck by three projectiles while sailing out of the strait, 17 nautical miles east of Oman's Khasab, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) said on Tuesday. No casualties or environmental impact have been reported, UKMTO said. (With input from agencies)

items.title: 12 assailants killed after Reko Diq convoy comes under attack in Chagai
items.description: QUETTA: Security forces killed 12 armed attackers following a terrorist attack on a convoy of vehicles from the Reko Diq copper and gold project, in the Chagai area on Monday. Security officials said a group of armed men attacked the convoy as it was travelling to Quetta from the project site. According to sources, unidentified attackers tried to intercept the convoy and opened heavy fire on it. “Around three dozen empty vehicles of the Reko Diq project were travelling to Quetta under security protection when they were attacked in the Nokacha area of Chagai,” an official said on condition of anonymity. He said that soon after the attack, security personnel escorting the convoy took positions and returned fire. A heavy exchange of fire continued for more than two hours, during which two security personnel were injured. Officials initially said that 11 terrorists had been killed at the scene, adding that arms and ammunition, including heavy weapons, were recovered from the attackers. However, Balochistan Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti later said 12 terrorists had been killed in the exchange of fire. Officials from the Reko Diq project did not respond to a request for comment. CM Bugti said intelligence-based targeted operations against terrorists were continuing successfully and consistently across the province. “There will be no negotiations with those who take up arms against the state and shed the blood of innocent citizens,” he wrote on X, adding that elements choosing the path of terrorism and violence would be dealt with according to the law. He said the state would not compromise on its writ or the protection of the lives and property of the people. CM Bugti said security forces and law enforcement agencies were conducting effective and coordinated operations to establish peace and stability in Balochistan. Indiscriminate action would be taken against terrorists and their facilitators, and every attempt to undermine peace in the province would be foiled, he added. Published in Dawn, September 1st, 2026

items.title: Video: Kidnappers threatened to kill us after one month — Rescued NYSC member
items.description: A rescued National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) member, David Ayodele, has recounted the harrowing experience he and other abductees endured after being kidnapped and taken into a forest in Kogi State. Ayodele said the kidnappers threatened to keep the victims in captivity for one month before killing them, while also warning that anyone who moved without permission would be shot. The corps member was among 15 NYSC members and six other Nigerians rescued from a kidnappers’ den in Ofu Local Government Area of Kogi State. He said the victims were abducted while travelling from Bayelsa State to Abuja after completing their NYSC orientation programme and undergoing relocation. Recounting the incident after his rescue, Ayodele said the driver of the vehicle attempted to escape when the kidnappers emerged, but the occupants were eventually forced out at gunpoint. “Driver tried to escape, but he said, Who’s the driver? Who’s the driver? And I held the driver, then they opened the door, and they started leading us to the bush while they were shooting, you know, rounds of bullets in the air,” he said. According to him, the victims were subjected to flogging, kicking and verbal abuse as they were forced deeper into the forest. “Then we made our way to the bush with flogging and kicking and shouting and stuff,” he said. Ayodele said the kidnappers later told the victims they would remain in the forest for a month before being killed. “We reached one kind of bushy area; they asked us to sit down, they asked us who would drink water, that we would be here for one month, so they would kill all of us,” he recounted. He said the threat left the abductees too frightened to move without permission. “They warned us that if anybody moved without permission that they will shoot the person, so none of us really attempted to move because of fear and stuff,” he said. The victims were subsequently made to trek for a considerable distance through the forest before security operatives eventually reached them. “So we moved a lot, a lot, a lot, a lot and then thank God the Nigerian Army came to meet us,” he said. Ayodele praised the security agencies involved in the rescue operation, including the Nigerian Army, police, Department of State Services and local hunters. He said he had completed his NYSC orientation programme in Bayelsa State before being relocated to Abuja. “I did my orientation camp in Bayelsa camp,” he said. We walked for a long time, and they threated to kill us. – Rescued corps members recount experience Video Credit : Defence News // X pic.twitter.com/sLow4ATMNP — Vanguard Newspapers (@vanguardngrnews) August 31, 2026 Explaining how he joined the vehicle that was later intercepted, Ayodele said corps members were transported in organised vehicles to various states after the orientation programme. “So, on our way from Bayelsa, because we did relocation back to Abuja, so we were going to Abuja from Bayelsa camp. There were organised vehicles going to different states, so luckily we saw an Abuja vehicle,” he said. The rescue brought an end to the ordeal of the 21 victims who had been held by the kidnappers in the Ofu area of Kogi State. The post Video: Kidnappers threatened to kill us after one month — Rescued NYSC member appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Dubai property no longer safe haven
items.description: KARACHI: The Gulf war has curbed the outflow of black money from Pakistan to Dubai, while funds already invested are returning and being diverted into property in the country, according to sources in the property and currency markets. Thousands of Pakistanis have invested hundreds of millions of dollars in Dubai, particularly in property. Pakistan was identified twice as the second-largest foreign investor in Dubai property. It was widely believed that black money created in Pakistan had a safe haven in Dubai and was a catalyst for property price hikes there. “About $60 million in illegal (or black) money is created in Pakistan per month and has been invested in Dubai, but this has now stopped,” said All Pakistan Builders Association Chairman Hassan Bakhshi. Currency dealers said the situation has reversed, with black money in Dubai stuck and recovery difficult due to the ongoing war. Pakistanis struggle to recover investments as black money fuels Karachi property rally “The higher remittances from Dubai reflect that Pakistanis are sending back their liquid assets to Pakistan,” said a currency dealer. The war has changed Dubai’s appeal as a destination for investment and tourism. Inflows from Dubai have increased . The impact is that illegal money being created in Pakistan has once again diverted towards the property business. “Property prices in Defence went up 50-60 per cent after the Gulf war started. Since the title of the Defence property is safe (meaning no double filing or fake dealing), most of the money is going towards the area,” said Mr Bakhshi. Not only was black money going to Dubai, but many tech companies had also shifted there before the war because of a hurdle-free business environment. They were also moving abroad due to frequent internet connectivity issues and excessive interference from the tax authorities. Thousands of Pakistanis were using Dubai as a third country and conducting legal business with countries such as India and Bangladesh. Now they are stuck and trying to recover their investment from Dubai, as the war-like situation still prevails. Currency dealers said that once the situation normalises, hundreds of millions of dollars would return to Pakistan from the Gulf, as Dubai has lost the confidence of foreign investors. Mr Bakhshi also endorsed reports that Pakistani investors were trying their best to recover their investments from Dubai, but property prices in the war-affected country have fallen to a minimum level. Property dealers said that prices in Pakistan have started to increase after the war, and trading has also increased. Both buying and selling have increased due to improved liquidity. “The government is also taking measures to boost the construction industry, and the rebound in property prices was the result of this effort. The property prices in other areas of Karachi have increased in the range of 20 to 25pc,” said Karim Dad, a property dealer. Published in Dawn, September 1st, 2026

items.title: Coopération bilatérale : : Le Système des Nations Unies s’aligne sur les nouvelles priorités du Burkina Faso
items.description: Le Premier ministre, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, a reçu en audience ce lundi 31 août 2026 le nouveau Coordonnateur-résident du Système des Nations Unies au Burkina Faso, Njoya Tikum. Cette première rencontre officielle a permis de poser les bases d'une coopération bilatérale redéfinie, désormais soumise à une exigence stricte de souveraineté nationale et d'impact réel pour les populations. Pour s'inscrire dans la dynamique de développement du pays, l'action des agences onusiennes devra s'aligner rigoureusement sur le nouveau référentiel national de développement : le Plan RELANCE 2026-2030. La Primature a servi de cadre, ce lundi 31 août 2026, à une rencontre diplomatique importante pour l'avenir de la coopération au développement au Burkina Faso. Le Premier ministre, le camarade Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, s'est entretenu avec Njoya Tikum, récemment nommé aux fonctions de Coordonnateur-résident du Système des Nations Unies, également Coordonnateur humanitaire et Agent habilité à la sécurité. Au-delà de la simple prise de contact, cette audience a permis de définir les orientations claires de la collaboration future. Le chef du gouvernement a réaffirmé la ferme disponibilité du pays à entretenir un dialogue constructif avec ses partenaires, mais à condition que celui-ci s'opère dans le respect absolu de la souveraineté nationale, des choix stratégiques de l'État burkinabè et des aspirations du peuple. Au cœur des échanges figurait la mise en œuvre du nouveau Cadre de coopération entre le Burkina Faso et les Nations Unies. Le gouvernement burkinabè a insisté sur la nécessité de l'inscrire en parfaite cohérence avec le Plan RELANCE 2026-2030, le nouveau référentiel qui oriente la planification nationale. Pour les autorités, les interventions étrangères ne doivent plus se déployer de manière dispersée, mais s'articuler étroitement avec les priorités définies par l'exécutif national. Le Premier ministre a rappelé qu'une coopération réussie est une coopération qui produit des résultats tangibles et mesurables, capables d'améliorer de façon durable les conditions de vie quotidiennes des Burkinabè. Cette orientation stratégique axée sur l'efficacité a reçu l'adhésion du nouveau Coordonnateur-résident. Njoya Tikum a réaffirmé la volonté du Système des Nations Unies de se mobiliser pleinement pour accompagner le pays sur ses chantiers prioritaires. Pour y parvenir, le diplomate onusien mise sur un renforcement de la coordination interne entre les différentes agences de l'ONU. Cette démarche de rationalisation des ressources doit permettre de rendre les programmes plus cohérents, d'éviter les doublons et de canaliser efficacement l'ensemble des efforts vers les objectifs de développement portés par le Burkina Faso. L’article Coopération bilatérale : : Le Système des Nations Unies s'aligne sur les nouvelles priorités du Burkina Faso est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Govt increases petrol price by Rs0.77, cuts high-speed diesel price by Rs1.03
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · "> The government on Monday raised the price of petrol by Rs0.77 per litre and cut that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.03 per litre. Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs342.79 per litre while HSD will cost Rs370.41 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on September 1 (Tuesday). The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Govt cuts arms licence issuance by over 90pc
items.description: • Only 5,700 non-prohibited-bore arms licences issued in 13 months, Senate body told • Tallal Chaudhry says 60pc of those involved in terrorism incidents in KP and Balochistan were Afghan nationals ISLAMABAD: The federal government has cut the issuance of non-prohibited-bore arms licences by more than 90 per cent, with only 5,700 licences issued over the past 13 months under strict criteria, the Senate Standing Committee on Interior and Narcotics Control was informed on Monday. Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry told the committee, which met under the chairmanship of Senator Faisal Saleem Rehman, that more than 100,000 arms licences had previously been issued annually. He said a police character certificate was now mandatory to ensure that people with criminal records did not obtain licences. A parliamentarian’s recommendation was also required, with each National Assembly constituency limited to five recommendations per month. The minister added that prohibited-bore licences were issued strictly to entitled persons, including parliamentarians, judges, army and police officers, and recipients of national awards. Officials said there was no policy for issuing business-category arms licences in Balochistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and the former Fata. The ministry would brief the committee on the procedure for dealing with special cases. On visas for Afghan nationals, Mr Chaudhry said no visa was issued without due diligence and that extensions were granted on a case-by-case basis, mainly on humanitarian grounds for students and those requiring medical treatment. He said around one million Afghans had been issued visas over two years when relations with the neighbouring country were normal. The National Database and Registration Authority (Nadra) informed the committee that Afghan visa applications were processed under 18 categories handled by the Ministry of Interior and four by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, mainly for businesspeople and students. However, delays occurred due to security clearances. Senator Talha Mahmood said there should be some relaxation in the visa policy for businessmen and students. Mr Chaudhry told the committee that 60 per cent of those involved in terrorism incidents in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan were Afghan nationals. “Afghanistan is our neighbour but its intentions are not right,” he said. He ad­­ded that Afghan nationals had also been involved in terrorism incidents in Islam­abad and in the murder of trader Aamir. The committee was informed that the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) does not routinely check passengers’ mobile phones or social media accounts at airports. “We do not check anyone’s mobile phone at the airport. Only those about whom we have information regarding human smuggling are checked. We also do not check the social media of any passenger,” an FIA official said. Mr Chaudhry, without naming any country, said, “When I went abroad with my family, all of our social media was checked.” The committee was briefed on an intelligence-based Sindh Police operation in District Shikarpur that resulted in the recovery of minor girl Huram Saeed Pathan, who was kidnapped from Karachi on March 28, 2026, and another trafficked victim, Jennifer Amir. Published in Dawn, September 1st, 2026

items.title: 'Technical fault': Driverless car crashes into police van in Islamabad
items.description: KARACHI: A video clip went viral on social media after a remote-controlled car crashed into a police van in Islamabad, reportedly due to a “technical fault” caused by an internet disruption. On Sunday, journalist Muhammad Aalijah uploaded a video on his official social media account showing him seated in the front passenger seat of a car at Islamabad’s D-Chowk, which appeared to be operated using a remote-control device. As Aalijah explains the car’s features and it moves forward, the steering wheel, controlled remotely by an operator, suddenly goes out of control. The car consequently bumps into a police van parked along the road. The video also shows Aalijah pulling the handbrake in an attempt to prevent the car from hitting the police van, but his efforts prove futile. Since being uploaded, the video has been widely circulated on social media, with users adding witty captions to the footage. When contacted, Aalijah told Dawn that he had been asked by technology enthusiast Ehsan Zafar of Abbottabad to report on his tech-based automated-driving innovation. “Everything was fine until a technical fault occurred due to an internet disruption, causing the car to go out of control and crash into a police vehicle,” he said. Aalijah explained that the car was controlled remotely over the internet and that a sudden loss of connection caused it to go out of control. In a social media post on Monday, Aalijah said his intention in making the video was “never to defame or target this young man”, who owned and operated the car. “The sole purpose was to raise awareness and urge people to remain cautious until any new experiment or technology has been thoroughly tested, proven safe and established as a complete success,” he said. “This was a message of caution, not an attempt to discredit anyone.” Sharing the video online, Aalijah said the car’s system was not yet “completely safe and reliable”. “The vehicle was being operated through satellite and internet connections, but during external control, it went out of control as soon as the internet connection was disconnected and collided with a police vehicle,” he wrote. The incident occurred in a high-security area with very little traffic. “If the same situation had occurred on a busy road, the consequences could have been extremely dangerous, even fatal,” he said. “This video is not criticism; it is a responsible effort to raise awareness and issue a warning — by all means, experiment, but ensure safety first,” he added. Self-driving memes take on a life of their own Meanwhile, the video has been widely shared on social media, with some users appreciating the journalist’s efforts to promote local talent, while others have responded with amusing remarks. “Certainly, there is no shortage of talent in Pakistan,” a user wrote, quoting Aalijah in a jibe. An internet user added that even AI panics in Pakistan when it sees the cops. Another user advised the car’s owner and tech innovator not to give up. “Funny for some, maybe, but I see a great effort. It failed today; yes, hiccups happen, but I know this young Pakistani will one day have a perfect solution.” Noting the huge public attention, a user said the video clip had the potential to become the next “international meme”.

items.title: Le dernier tango de «La Pulga» avec l’Albiceleste
items.description: Après plus de deux décennies sous le maillot de l’Argentine, Lionel Messi a annoncé, ce lundi 31 août 2026, sa retraite internationale. À 39 ans, l’octuple Ballon d’Or quitte l’Albiceleste avec une gibecière bien pleine, où trône notamment le trophée mondial en 2022 et deux Copa América. Mais le point sombre du tableau est, sans aucun doute, cette défaite en finale du Mondial 2026, contre l'Espagne de Lamine Yamal, ce bébé à qui il a donné son bain en 2007, lors d'une séance photo caritative de l'Unicef. Un clin d'oeil du destin qui a peut-être pesé dans la décision de «La Pulga» de se retirer d'une scène internationale du football désormais dominée par des jeunes loups aux dents longues. Sans oublier le décès, le 8 août 2026, à l'âge de 68 ans, de Jorge Messi, le père de Lionel. Ainsi, l’un des plus célèbres «Numéros 10» argentins du football actuel, après Maradona, range son maillot avec l’Albiceleste. Ce n’est un secret pour personne, ce cauchemar des défenses adverses, que ce soit avec le club de sa vie Barcelone, ou durant son passage épisodique au Paris Saint- Germain ou encore avec l’Inter Miami où il évolue actuellement, a toujours été l’attraction. Haut comme trois pommes, il est irrésistible par ses dribbles chaloupés, ses coups de patte venus d’une autre planète, mais aussi par son humilité déconcertante. C’était un extra-terrestre qui avait le don de porter, à lui seul, tout une équipe vers la victoire et de décider, quand il le veut et où il le veut, du sort d’un match. Rares de défenseurs, notamment ceux du Real de Madrid, l’historique rival du Barça, pouvaient contenir le remuant et imprévisible Leo Messi durant les 90 minutes réglementaires d’un match de football. Dans son jardin du Camp Nou dont il maîtrise chaque centimètre de pelouse, il soulevait tout le peuple catalan qu’il comblait de gestes fous. Certes, l’éternelle rivalité entre Lionel Messi et Cristiano Ronaldo, 41 ans, qui s’était plus ou moins étiolée avec le départ de CR7 de la Liga, en 2018, mais qui s’est poursuivies au niveau des fans des deux stars, sur les réseaux sociaux tout comme dans les médias, continue, et continuera sans doute d’alimenter les débats. Mais, ce retrait, bien que partiel, du messie argentin du football marque la fin d’une époque. En attendant que le Portugais Cristiano Ronaldo, qui fait, aujourd’hui, les beaux jours de Al-Nassr FC, le club saoudien, décide, lui aussi, de tourner le dos à la sélection nationale, surtout après un mondial américain décevant, qu’il a traversé comme une ombre, c’est une ère footballistique qui tire, inexorablement, vers la fin. Considérés comme les deux meilleurs de leur génération, «La Pulga» et CR7 peuvent se targuer d’un palmarès stratosphérique. Mais, il commencent à subir la trahison du poids de l’âge, doublée de l’usure inévitable de ces «classicos» qui étaient très attendus dans le monde entier et qu’il ne fallait perdre à aucun prix. Quel héritage Lionel Messi laisse-t-il aux jeunes joueurs argentins qui auront le devoir de faire briller l’Argentine en Copa America et de ramener leur pays sur le toit du monde après 1978, 1986 et 2022? D’ores et déjà, les héritiers de Messi sont conscients que remplacer un footballeur, que dis-je, un génie comme leur capitaine, n’est pas une entreprise facile. S’ils doivent travailler pour viser son talent, ils doivent surtout chercher à cultiver l’humilité et la constance du grand meneur d’hommes, qu’était le capitaine argentin. Le malheur des uns faisant le bonheur des autres, c’est l’Inter Miami qui se frotte les mains, le club américain pouvant désormais jouir de son chouchou, à plein temps! Par Wakat Séra L’article Le dernier tango de «La Pulga» avec l’Albiceleste est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Barrage de Pô : un homme d’une quarantaine d’années porté disparu dans les eaux
items.description: La tristesse et la consternation ont envahi la ville de Pô ce lundi 31 août 2026, à la suite de la disparition brutale d'un maçon de 40 ans, père de quatre enfants, dans les eaux du tout nouveau barrage de Kapro. Selon les informations rapportées par le média local Les Infos du Sud , le drame est survenu dans l'après-midi lors d'une baignade qui a mal tourné après une partie de pêche. Les autorités provinciales, sous la direction du Haut-Commissaire du Nahouri, se sont immédiatement rendues sur place pour organiser les premières recherches en attendant l’intervention d'une équipe de plongeurs spécialisés attendue de Ouagadougou. Un après-midi de détente a basculé dans l'horreur à Pô, chef-lieu de la province du Nahouri. Le lundi 31 août 2026, aux environs de 15 heures, Issa .B, un maçon de profession âgé d'une quarantaine d'années, marié et père de quatre enfants, a disparu dans les eaux du barrage de Kapro. Comme le relate le journal en ligne Les Infos du Sud , la victime, résidant au secteur 1 de la ville, s'était rendue sur le site en compagnie d'un camarade pour une partie de pêche. Le récit d'un sauvetage impossible Une fois l'activité de pêche achevée, Issa .B a décidé de se baigner dans le plan d'eau. Malheureusement, le quadragénaire s'est rapidement retrouvé en difficulté au milieu du bassin. Témoin direct de la scène, son compagnon de pêche a courageusement tenté de lui porter secours et de le ramener sur la terre ferme. Face à la force de l'élément aquatique et malgré des efforts désespérés, il a dû se résoudre à abandonner sa tentative pour appeler à l'aide, alertant les riverains et les passants situés aux alentours. La nouvelle s'est rapidement propagée, provoquant une forte mobilisation de la population locale. Très vite, les plus hautes autorités de la province ont convergé vers le site du drame pour témoigner de leur soutien et coordonner la situation. Étaient notamment présents sur les berges le Haut-Commissaire de la province du Nahouri, Sié Aristide Mohamed Kam, le président de la délégation spéciale de Pô, ainsi que le procureur du Faso près le Tribunal de première instance de Pô. L’attente douloureuse des secours spécialisés La recherche du corps a cependant mis en lumière les difficultés logistiques des unités de secours locales. Alertés en premier lieu, les sapeurs-pompiers de Manga n'ont pas pu se déployer immédiatement sur le site, étant déjà mobilisés sur un autre théâtre d'opération d'urgence. Face à cette indisponibilité, ils ont pris attache avec leurs collègues de Ouagadougou pour mettre sur pied une équipe de recherche adéquate. Selon les déclarations du Haut-Commissaire Sié Aristide Mohamed Kam, cette équipe spécialisée de secours est attendue dans la nuit afin de pouvoir entamer des fouilles subaquatiques méthodiques dès le lendemain matin. Vers 19 heures, la nuit tombante a contraint les autorités et les nombreux curieux à quitter le site dans une profonde affliction. Un ouvrage récent sous les projecteurs Ce terrible événement suscite d’autant plus d'émoi que le barrage de Kapro est une infrastructure extrêmement récente. Son inauguration officielle remonte au 25 juillet 2026, soit à peine plus d’un mois avant le drame. Pour de nombreux observateurs, cette disparition tragique vient cruellement rappeler la nécessité absolue de mettre en place des dispositifs de surveillance et de sensibiliser les populations aux dangers inhérents à la baignade non surveillée dans les nouveaux aménagements hydrauliques de la région. L’article Barrage de Pô : un homme d’une quarantaine d’années porté disparu dans les eaux est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Full text of Xi Jinping's signed article in Egyptian media
items.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday published a signed article titled "Celebrating 70 Years of Solidarity, China and Egypt Embark on a New Journey" in Al-Ahram, Al-Akhbar and Al-Gomhuria ahead of his arrival in Egypt for a state visit. The following is the full text of the article: Celebrating 70 Years of Solidarity, China and Egypt Embark on a New Journey H.E. Xi Jinping President of the People's Republic of China For Al-Ahram, Al-Akhbar, and Al-Gomhuria At the invitation of His Excellency President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, I will be paying a state visit to Egypt and, as President of the People's Republic of China, setting foot for the second time on this land nourished by the Nile. Just as an Egyptian proverb reads, "Once you drink from the Nile, you are destined to return." During my last visit ten years ago, I was deeply impressed by the time-honored, profound civilization of this country, together with its booming vitality and upward momentum. This time, I look forward to renewing the friendship and working together with President El-Sisi to explore ways of cooperation and map out a new blueprint for deepening the China-Egypt comprehensive strategic partnership. As a Chinese saying goes, "A partnership forged with the right approach defies distance." Known for their age-old civilizations, China and Egypt have each contributed an invaluable intellectual legacy and splendid cultural heritage to the progress of humanity. The Yangtze River and the Yellow River gave birth to the Chinese civilization, and the Nile was the cradle of the ancient Egyptian civilization. With porcelain and silk sailing the seas and traversing the deserts, the vast geographical distance never kept our two civilizations from appreciating each other, and friendly exchanges along the millennium-old ancient Silk Road never stopped. Chinese silk, porcelain, and paper-making, smelting and casting techniques made their way westward, while Egyptian aromatics, glassware and calendrical knowledge journeyed over thousands of miles eastward. The Chinese artifacts unearthed in Fustat attest to the close bonds and deep friendship that have existed between our peoples since ancient times. Seventy years ago, China and Egypt officially established diplomatic relations, marking the start of New China's friendly cooperation with Arab and African countries. For seven decades, the China-Egypt relationship has braved wind and rain, and withstood the test of the changing international landscape. It has stayed on the right course, remained robust as ever, and sustained a strong momentum. It is a fine example for China's cooperation with Arab states and Africa on the whole, and for friendship, solidarity and collaboration between developing countries. — China and Egypt have always been close brothers standing by each other. In the struggle for national independence and against imperialism and colonialism, the people of our two countries forged profound friendship. China firmly supported Egypt's sovereignty over the Suez Canal, and Egypt, alongside the majority of Asian, African, and Latin American and Caribbean countries, voted unequivocally in favor of the restoration of the lawful seat of the People's Republic of China in the United Nations. Currently, our two sides firmly support each other in pursuing development paths suited to our respective national conditions, and firmly support each other on core interests and major concerns. All this has laid a solid foundation for the China-Egypt comprehensive strategic partnership. — China and Egypt have always been reliable partners in win-win cooperation. Egypt is China's major trading and investment partner in the Arab world and Africa, and one of the first countries to participate in Belt and Road cooperation. As early as ten years ago, President El-Sisi and I jointly unveiled the China-Egypt Suez Economic and Trade Cooperation Zone. The project has drawn substantial investment, created a large number of local jobs, and helped in Egypt's endeavor to expedite its modernization. In other fields, fruits of mutually beneficial cooperation -- from Africa's tallest building and first intercity electric light rail built in Egypt by Chinese enterprises, to fresh Egyptian oranges heading for the Chinese market as the first African produce to capitalize on China's zero-tariff policy for the African countries having diplomatic relations with it -- are shared by countless households in both countries. — China and Egypt have always been the role models of friendship and mutual learning. Egypt is the first among both Arab nations and African countries to sign an agreement on cultural cooperation with New China, and our people-to-people exchanges have been diverse and vibrant. The Grand Egyptian Museum is a must-visit for Chinese tourists, so much so that the exhibition "The Civilization of Ancient Egypt" in Shanghai Museum saw tickets sell out in seconds. In Egypt, the Chinese language is taught in more than 40 middle schools, and cooperation with China on vocational education has benefited numerous Egyptians. Across time and space, the two civilizations have been reaching out to each other, adding new chapters of everlasting friendship between the two peoples. — China and Egypt have always been sincere friends committed to equality and mutual trust. At the Bandung Conference in 1955, our two countries actively supported the anti-imperial and anti-colonial struggle, and jointly advanced Asian-African solidarity. Today, China and Egypt have shared goals and common aspiration in upholding international order, championing fairness and justice, and practicing multilateralism. Both sides firmly support the just cause of the Palestinian people in restoring their legitimate national rights, and both are committed to facilitating the political settlement of hotspot issues and realizing peace and stability in the region. This demonstrates our commitment, as Global South countries, to seeking strength through unity and upholding fairness and justice. Our two countries are each at a critical stage of development and national revitalization. China saw its 15th Five-Year Plan for economic and social development getting off to a good start, and is striving to open up new ground in Chinese modernization. Egypt is making vigorous efforts in building the New Republic and forging ahead toward its Vision 2030. The Chinese side is ready to work with the Egyptian side to deepen the comprehensive strategic partnership, advance the building of a community with a shared future between the two countries, and join hands in realizing modernization. We need to enhance mutual trust and serve as a model in carrying forward friendship. The friendship between our two countries was forged by the elder generations of our leaders. It is our honor and responsibility to carry forward, develop and promote this friendship. Our two sides should continue supporting each other on core interests and major concerns, and deepen exchanges and cooperation at various levels and across all sectors to ensure that the baton of friendship is passed on from generation to generation. We need to pursue mutual benefit and win-win cooperation and set a benchmark for joint development. China has the world's largest and most complete industrial system, and is strong in capital, technology and equipment. Egypt has a large population, abundant resources and a vast market. Our two sides should forge greater synergy in development strategies, engage in high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, proactively tap the potential and expand the scope of pragmatic collaboration in a bid to provide sustained impetus to the mutually beneficial cooperation. We need to take pride in who we are while setting an example for exchanges and mutual learning. As two great civilizations, China and Egypt should champion equality, mutual learning, dialogue and inclusiveness among civilizations, implement the Global Civilization Initiative, actively protect humanity's cultural heritage, and jointly promote the harmonious coexistence of various civilizations. Our two sides should deepen exchanges and cooperation in areas such as education, tourism, science and technology, health, sports and archaeology, forge a stronger bond of mutual understanding and affinity between our two peoples, with a view to injecting new momentum into the China-Egypt comprehensive strategic partnership, and harnessing the strengths of diverse civilizations to promote the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. We need to press ahead side by side and be pioneers in upholding fairness and justice. Profound changes unseen in a century are unfolding at a faster pace, amid a volatile international landscape. As both major developing countries and important Global South nations, China and Egypt should vigorously uphold world peace and stability, and international fairness and justice by practicing true multilateralism, enhancing multilateral coordination, and working together to deliver on the four global initiatives on development, security, civilization and governance. We need to join hands to lead the way in China-Arab and China-Africa cooperation. As a major country in both the Arab world and Africa, Egypt plays an important role in promoting the collective cooperation between China and Arab states, and between China and African countries. The Chinese side is ready to work with the Egyptian side to enhance the demonstration effect of our well-established cooperation, leverage Egypt's unique location in linking the Arab world and reaching across the African continent, further implement the proposal on building "five cooperation frameworks" between China and Arab states and follow up on the ten partnership actions for modernization between China and Africa. This will ensure that China-Arab and China-Africa cooperation keeps pace with the times, makes steady progress and goes a long way. For 70 years, China and Egypt have stood by each other rain or shine. Now our two countries are embarking on a new journey with enterprise and fortitude. The Chinese side is ready to work with the Egyptian side to stay true to the shared aspiration of our two countries, build on our past achievements, support each other and forge ahead on the path toward prosperity and rejuvenation, and strive for a better tomorrow in both our respective national development and our bilateral relations.

items.title: Chinese town emerges as world’s guitar capital
items.description: ZHENG’AN: It doesn’t take long to gue­ss the main industry of the Chinese town of Zheng’an. A giant guitar sculpture dominates the central square, guitar murals adorn walls and pavements and even the rubbish bins are shaped like guitars. This corner of the southwest province of Guizhou produces one in every seven of the instruments sold worldwide. A decade ago, it had no guitar-making industry to speak of at all. There are hundreds of specialised manufacturing towns in China, producing items ranging from bicycles to socks. But the speed and scale of Zheng’an’s rise make it an example of the impact of China’s industrial strategy when a combination of local and central government investment is deployed to maximise favourable local conditions. For years, the town’s working-age residents left to find employment in factories in Guangdong, southern China’s manufacturing hub. Among them was Zheng Chuanjiu, who eventually started his own guitar-making business in the provincial capital Guangzhou. “The company was doing pretty well at that time and most of our staff in Guangzhou were also our fellow villagers from Zheng’an,” the founder of Shenqu Guitar said. In 2012, Zheng’an local authorities rolled out an initiative called “return the phoenix to the nest”, to encourage skilled migrant workers to return home and start businesses. “The county officials reached out to us. They wanted us to come back and develop the industry,” Zheng said. Shenqu became the first guitar manufacturer to settle in Zheng’an’s new economic zone. Published in Dawn, September 1st, 2026

items.title: Niger: après la mutinerie à Niamey, les raisons de la colère dans les rangs de l’armée
items.description: Au Niger, journée calme ce lundi 31 août à Niamey, après un week-end marqué par des tirs. Ils ont commencé dans la nuit de vendredi à samedi et se sont poursuivis dans la journée de samedi. De violents affrontements ont opposé des soldats mutins, d’un côté, à la garde présidentielle, appuyée par les forces russes de l’Africa Corps, de l’autre. Depuis, aucun bilan officiel n’a été communiqué. Le général Abdourahamane Tiani, à la tête du CNSP, ne s’est pas exprimé publiquement. Les autorités parlent d’un « mouvement d’humeur ». Beaucoup de zones d’ombre persistent, notamment sur les raisons qui ont conduit à ces événements.

items.title: « Ne bouffe pas le wack, les gens se flattent… » : Adja Salmata Soré appelle à ne pas négliger le culte traditionnel
items.description: Dans une déclaration consacrée aux réalités du monde spirituel, Adja Salmata Soré a appelé ceux qui hésitent à pratiquer le culte traditionnel à ne pas rejeter systématiquement cette dimension. « Ne bouffe pas le wack, ceux qui vous disent ça vous flattent», a-t-elle lancé à l’endroit de ceux qui hésitent à s’engager dans les pratiques traditionnelles. Selon elle, de nombreux problèmes qui affectent les familles ne seraient pas uniquement liés aux réalités visibles. « Je demande à Dieu de vous donner nos yeux pour que vous voyez un peu ce qui se passe dans la vie », a-t-elle déclaré, évoquant ce qu’elle présente comme les réalités du monde spirituel. Adja Salmata Soré estime que les difficultés familiales sont aujourd’hui profondes et nombreuses. « Le mal est très profond. Sur 10 maisons, 9 ont des problèmes : des problèmes de couples, des mésententes, de la haine, des divorces. Des frères ne se parlent pas, des pères et des fils ne se parlent plus. C’est compliqué », a-t-elle ajouté. Une sortie qui relance le débat sur la place des pratiques et croyances traditionnelles dans la société contemporaine, notamment face aux difficultés sociales et familiales. Tiwana 24 L’article « Ne bouffe pas le wack, les gens se flattent… » : Adja Salmata Soré appelle à ne pas négliger le culte traditionnel est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Séno/Falagountou: le PDS remet 60 motos, deux drones et 5 millions FCFA de carburant à la gendarmerie et aux VDP
items.description: Le président de la Délégation spéciale communale de Falagountou, Alou Goro, a remis, lundi, 60 motocyclettes, deux drones de surveillance et du carburant d’une valeur de 5 millions de FCFA au profit de la Brigade territoriale de gendarmerie et des Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP) communaux de Falagountou, afin de renforcer leurs capacités opérationnelles. Les 60 motocyclettes sont destinées à renforcer la mobilité et les capacités opérationnelles des forces engagées dans la sécurisation de la commune. En plus des motos, deux drones ont été remis aux bénéficiaires. Ces équipements devraient contribuer à améliorer les capacités de surveillance et de renseignement, notamment dans le suivi des mouvements et la détection d’éventuelles menaces dans la zone. La dotation comprend également des cartes de carburant d’une valeur totale de 5 millions de FCFA. Ce soutien vise à faciliter les déplacements des éléments de la gendarmerie et des VDP dans le cadre de leurs missions de sécurisation et de protection des populations. À travers cette dotation, les autorités communales entendent accompagner davantage les forces combattantes dans l’accomplissement de leurs missions. Les moyens remis devraient permettre aux bénéficiaires d’améliorer leur mobilité, leur capacité d’intervention et la couverture sécuritaire de la commune. La remise de ces équipements traduit ainsi la volonté des autorités locales de contribuer, aux côtés des forces de défense et de sécurité et des VDP, au renforcement de la sécurité et à la protection des populations de Falagountou. Elle constitue également un appel à une utilisation responsable et efficace de ces moyens au service de la paix et de la quiétude dans la commune. Agence d’Information du Burkina AMM/bak L’article Séno/Falagountou: le PDS remet 60 motos, deux drones et 5 millions FCFA de carburant à la gendarmerie et aux VDP est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Chantier de la route Bérégadougou-Orodara : Trois prévenus risque 5 ans de prison pour tentative de vol de gasoil
items.description: Le Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Banfora a examiné, le 25 août 2026, une affaire de vol aggravé et de tentative de vol aggravé mettant en cause trois hommes travaillant dans une même entreprise à Bérégadougou et chargée du bitumage de la route Bérégadougou-Orodara. Tous trois ont comparu à la barre, avec des versions parfois concordantes, mais aussi des divergences sur le rôle joué par chacun. Cette affaire intervient alors que, trois semaines plus tôt, le journal «Le Pays» avait déjà consacré une de ses rubriques à la question du trafic et des tentatives de détournement de gasoil dans cette entreprise en charge des travaux de construction de la route Banfora-Orodara, mettant en lumière les pratiques entourant ce phénomène. Au banc des prévenus, figurent JV, chauffeur, SR, également chauffeur, et MS, gardien. Tous sont âgés au moins d'une trentaine d'années et pères de famille. Si les deux premiers reconnaissent leur implication dans le projet, MS conteste avoir donné son accord à l'opération. Selon les éléments présentés à l'audience, l'idée de soustraire du gasoil aurait été soufflée à SR par un ami chauffeur à la SN-SOSUCO. Ce dernier lui aurait expliqué qu'il s'adonnait régulièrement à cette pratique sans avoir été inquiété. Confronté aux difficultés financières, notamment à la grossesse de son épouse et à l'impossibilité d'obtenir un crédit, SR affirme avoir finalement cédé à la tentation. Pour mettre son projet à exécution, il aurait sollicité JV et approché MS qui, lui, travaillait comme gardien sur le site de la base vie de l'entreprise. D'après SR, ce dernier devait fermer les yeux sur leur passage en contrepartie d'une part du produit du vol. Dans la nuit du 24 juillet 2026, les acolytes auraient ainsi tenté de passer à l'action. SR aurait prévenu MS de leur arrivée avant de prendre la direction du garage à bord d'un tricycle, en compagnie de JV et d'un présumé receleur. Mais l'opération ne se déroule pas comme prévu. Les occupants du tricycle constatent qu'ils sont suivis par un véhicule. Arrivés aux abords de la base vie, ils aperçoivent également MS qui leur adresse un signal lumineux avec sa torche. Prenant ce geste pour un avertissement, ils décident finalement de rebrousser chemin et d'abandonner leur projet. Mais c'était sans compter avec la clairvoyance des gendarmes de Bérégadougou qui procéderont à l'interpellation. A la barre, JV livre une version globalement proche de celle de SR, tout en soutenant qu'il avait demandé l'abandon de l'opération avant même leur arrivée sur les lieux. Il affirme notamment qu'au moment où il a souhaité quitter le tricycle, le présumé receleur aurait accéléré, l’empêchant ainsi de descendre. MS, en revanche, nie toute participation au projet. Il reconnaît avoir été approché par SR, qui lui aurait parlé de son intention de voler du gasoil. Il affirme même lui avoir demandé combien de bidons il comptait emporter. Selon lui, SR aurait évoqué neuf bidons de 20 litres. Mais MS soutient n'avoir jamais accepté de participer à l'opération. Le soir des faits, il dit avoir reçu un appel provenant d'un numéro inconnu l'informant que des personnes étaient en route vers le site. Il affirme ensuite avoir aperçu un tricycle et utilisé sa torche pour identifier ses occupants, sans savoir, selon sa version, qu'ils venaient pour voler. Une explication qui ne convainc pas le parquet. Pour le procureur du Faso près le TGI de Banfora, les trois prévenus étaient bel et bien liés par un même dessein. L'intervention des gendarmes qui suivaient les suspects ainsi que le signal lumineux lancé par MS auraient empêché l'opération d'aller à son terme. Le représentant du ministère public s'est particulièrement attardé sur le cas de JV, ancien détenu condamné en 2023 à trois ans de prison et ayant bénéficié d'une remise de peine le 9 avril 2026. Après sa libération, il avait retrouvé un emploi de chauffeur. Pour le procureur, ce parcours aurait dû inciter JV à éviter toute nouvelle implication dans une affaire pénale. « Vous avez eu la chance de sortir de prison grâce à une remise de peine. Vous avez eu la chance de trouver très vite un travail stable qui paie bien », lui a-t-il notamment lancé, déplorant qu'il se soit à nouveau retrouvé mêlé à une telle affaire. Au terme des débats, le parquet a demandé au tribunal de déclarer les trois prévenus coupables. Il a requis contre SR, poursuivi pour tentative de vol aggravé, cinq ans d’emprisonnement dont trois ans ferme, assortis d'une amende d'un million de F CFA ferme. Pour JV, également poursuivi pour tentative de vol aggravé, le procureur a requis cinq ans de prison ferme et un million de F CFA d'amende ferme. Enfin, contre MS, poursuivi pour complicité de tentative de vol aggravé, le parquet a sollicité cinq ans d’emprisonnement dont trois ans ferme, ainsi qu'une amende d'un million de F CFA ferme. Le tribunal n'a pas rendu sa décision à l'issue de l'audience.
